description: Keeps every pinned version current: GitHub Actions (pinned to commit hashes), the locked Python dependencies, the Dockerfile's base images, the Terraform providers, and the pins no built-in reader knows (infra/kind/pins.env, the Makefile's images, the gitleaks version, the pinned MCP server).

One grouped pull request per group, on the first day of the month. The hourly limit of the recommended preset is off, since one day a month is the limit; at most 20 are open at once. Nothing is merged by Renovate: a session or the owner merges, as the plan's Part A says.
A new pin in pins.env, the Makefile or a workflow needs a reader here; tests/test_renovate_config.py fails when a pin of a shape it knows has none.
Advisories are GitHub's: its own security updates open those pull requests, so Renovate's are off and no advisory gets two.

customManagers.description: An image pinned by tag and digest in a KEY=value line.
The three images of the documentation toolchain, wherever the Makefile or a script names one (a default and the comment that repeats it move together).
A version on the line under a '# renovate: datasource=... depName=...' comment; a KEY_DIGEST line right below it is the image's digest.
The MCP server that npx runs at a pinned version.

packageRules.description: A release is proposed once it is a week old: a bad one has usually been withdrawn by then. Only for sources that say when a release was made.
One pull request for the GitHub Actions.
One pull request for the Python dependencies.
One pull request for the Dockerfile's base images.
prBodyNotes: CI does not build the image. Before merging, run `make deploy` on this branch: it builds the image and starts the services from it.

packageRules.description: One pull request for the documentation toolchain.
prBodyNotes: Structurizr and gitleaks run in required checks. Pandoc and Mermaid run only in `Docs / Architecture PDF`, which is not required: read its result before merging.

packageRules.description: The MCP server runs on the owner's laptop through npx, with control of a browser: its update is the owner's to read and merge.
prBodyNotes: This package runs on the owner's laptop with control of a browser. The owner reads the release notes and merges; a session does not.

packageRules.description: One pull request for Terraform and its providers.
prBodyNotes: CI does not run Terraform. Before merging, run `make azure-plan` and read the plan.

packageRules.description: One pull request for the local platform. CI never starts it, so green checks prove nothing here.
prBodyNotes: CI does not start the kind platform. Before merging, run `make up` and `make smoke` on this branch, put what they printed in a comment, and bring the versions table in `infra/kind/README.md` up to date.

The images in `pins.env` that a chart runs (`X_IMAGE_TAG` and `X_IMAGE_DIGEST`) are the tags that chart version installs by default. A tag Renovate proposes that is not the chart's own belongs with a newer chart: leave it, or move the chart too, and read the chart's defaults again with the command in `infra/kind/README.md`.

packageRules.description: approver-policy is built against one cert-manager release (the plan's backlog records v0.28.0 against v1.21.2), so the two charts and cert-manager's images arrive in one pull request. This rule comes after the 'kind platform' one so that its group wins.
prBodyNotes: approver-policy and cert-manager arrive together. Look up which cert-manager version the new approver-policy release is built against (its release notes or go.mod), and move both charts, and the images of cert-manager's components, to versions that agree. CI does not start the platform; run `make up` and `make smoke` on this branch and put what they printed in a comment.

packageRules.description: promtool, the rule checker CI runs with make alerts, comes from the Prometheus image: it follows the Prometheus version the kube-prometheus-stack chart installs.
prBodyNotes: This image is the rule checker CI runs with `make alerts`. Keep it at the Prometheus version the kube-prometheus-stack chart in `infra/kind/pins.env` installs: a newer checker accepts rules the cluster's Prometheus may not.

packageRules.description: The test database and the cluster's database carry the same PostgreSQL, pgvector and OS release, so they arrive together.
A PostgreSQL major upgrade means ingesting the knowledge store again (the plan's follow-ups): by hand, in a step.
The Kubernetes minor follows what is generally available on AKS: by hand.
CI's Helm is the version infra/kind/README.md documents for the laptop, and a test compares the two: by hand.
The Python minor is a step's decision (requires-python, the image and .python-version move together).
